Ministry to the Saints
MIN-is-tree too thuh SAYNTS
noun (Christian service)
From Greek diakonia, service or ministration, rendered ministry; the service rendered to the saints, the household of faith.

📖 Biblical Definition

Ministry to the Saints is the diakonia, the practical service, rendered by believers to their fellow believers as members of one body. Paul went up to Jerusalem "to minister unto the saints" (Rom 15:25), carrying the relief of the Gentile churches to the poor brethren there. He commends the house of Stephanas, "that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints" (1 Cor 16:15), and he assures the Hebrews that "God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister" (Heb 6:10). Such ministry is no incidental kindness but the very fruit of saving grace, the love that proves a living faith. It is service rendered to Christ Himself, for what is done to the least of His brethren is done unto Him. Distinct from the world's philanthropy, it is directed first to the household of God, "especially unto them who are of the household of faith" (Gal 6:10). This dictionary confesses that genuine ministry to the saints flows from regenerate hearts, is wrought by the Spirit, and is so esteemed by God that He counts it done unto His own name.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The practical service (diakonia) rendered by believers to fellow believers as members of one body; a fruit of grace which God Himself esteems as labor of love shown toward His name.

expand to see more

MINISTRY TO THE SAINTS, noun. The practical service rendered by believers to their fellow believers.

Exemplified by Paul going to Jerusalem "to minister unto the saints" with the relief Collection.

Seen also in the house of Stephanas, "addicted" to the ministry of the saints.

It requires love proved in deed toward the household of faith, and it forbids a faith barren of works.

God counts it "love, which ye have shewed toward his name," and is not unrighteous to forget it.

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 15:25 — "But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints."

1 Cor 16:15 — "I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)."

Heb 6:10 — "For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister."

Gal 6:10 — "As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the danger is to dissolve Christian service into mere humanitarianism that loses its God-ward and church-ward direction.

expand to see more

There is no ideological redefinition of this doctrine, but it is often diluted. The modern impulse is to collapse ministry to the saints into generic humanitarianism, as though serving anyone for any reason were the same thing. Scripture orders the love: "especially unto them who are of the household of faith." While believers are to do good unto all men, their first and peculiar obligation is to the brethren, the members of Christ's body, the saints with whom they share one Lord, one faith, one baptism.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the God-ward weight of such service: it is "labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name." What is done to the saints is reckoned as done to Christ, and God is not unrighteous to forget it. This lifts the meanest act of service—the meal carried, the burden borne, the gift sent—into an act of worship, performed unto the Lord and remembered by Him. To recover this is to see Christian charity not as detached benevolence but as the living fruit of grace within the body.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Greek diakonia, service or ministration, directed to the hagioi, the saints.

expand to see more

Ministry renders the Greek diakonia, service, ministration, the work of a diakonos.

Saints renders hagioi, the holy ones, those set apart unto God in Christ.

Rom 15:25 uses the verb diakonōn, ministering, of Paul's service with the relief.

Heb 6:10 names it ergon and kopos tēs agapēs, work and labour of love.

The terms root such service in grace received and directed first to the household of faith.

Usage

"Paul's ministry to the saints carried the Gentile churches' relief to the poor believers at Jerusalem."

"The house of Stephanas gave themselves to the ministry of the saints as the firstfruits of Achaia."

"God remembers every act of ministry to the saints as love shown toward His own name."
